findings.explanation: The ServiceNow `task_sla` table has no `sla_start_time` or `due_at` column. The real columns are `start_time`, `planned_end_time` (labelled "Breach time"), `has_breached` (the breach flag), `stage`, `percentage`, `business_percentage` and `task` (the reference to the parent incident or task). A reader mapping fields from this text will not find them.
findings.quote: Ingest SLA task rows with `sla_start_time`, `planned_end_time` (or `due_at`), breach flag, and parent incident.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the real columns: `start_time`, `planned_end_time`, `has_breached`, `stage`, `percentage` / `business_percentage`, `task` (parent reference) and `sla` (the SLA definition).

findings.explanation: The SLA engine already maintains "Actual elapsed percentage" (`percentage`) and "Business elapsed percentage" (`business_percentage`), both net of pause time. A wall-clock ratio of now minus start over breach time minus start overstates progress for SLAs on business-hours schedules and for paused SLAs. The text also never says to restrict to `stage=in_progress`.
findings.quote: Compute percent of SLA window consumed. Alert when elapsed ≥80% and breach has not occurred.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `business_percentage` (or `percentage` for 24x7 SLAs) taken from the latest record per task_sla `sys_id`, filtered to `stage=in_progress` and `has_breached=false`. Alert at 80% or higher, tuned per SLA definition.

findings.explanation: The text contains two concatenated copies of Steps 1 to 4, and the second is generic boilerplate (a `tstats` count compared with a "vendor admin UI", HTTP 401/429 troubleshooting, an "entity" the SPL never uses). It also never says that `task_sla` is not a default Splunk_TA_snow input and must be added as a custom table input. The add-on indexes a new event on every record update, so without a per-`sys_id` latest step a 24-hour window returns duplicate and stale snapshots.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one set of steps: add a `task_sla` table input in Splunk_TA_snow (sourcetype `snow:task_sla`), set its poll interval, reduce to the latest event per `sys_id`, schedule every 15 minutes, and throttle on `task`. Remove the generic troubleshooting block.

findings.explanation: The false positives refer to `host`, maintenance windows and synthetic probes, which have nothing to do with ticket SLAs. The real sources of false at-risk rows are missing.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `itsm` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: paused or on-hold SLAs whose wall-clock percentage keeps rising; business-hours schedules where wall-clock elapsed time exceeds business elapsed time; stale snapshot events for SLAs that have since completed or been cancelled; SLAs reset or retroactively recalculated after a priority change; and duplicate SLA definitions attached to the same task.

findings.explanation: The data sources list incident data, but the SPL reads only `snow:task_sla` and never joins incidents. They also do not name any of the task_sla fields the detection depends on.
findings.quote: ServiceNow incident + SLA task / task_sla (`sourcetype=snow:task_sla` or equivalent)
findings.suggested_fix: List `index=itsm sourcetype=snow:task_sla` with fields `sys_id`, `task`, `sla`, `stage`, `has_breached`, `start_time`, `planned_end_time`, `business_percentage`. Mention `snow:incident` only if it is joined for priority or assignment group.

findings.explanation: None of the references describes the ServiceNow Task SLA table or its timing fields, which this UC depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the ServiceNow Task SLA table documentation (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/it-service-management/service-level-management/r_TaskSLATable.html).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL references `breach_time`, `sla_start_time`, `parent`, `number` and `sla_type`, which are not task_sla columns. The ServiceNow dictionary has `has_breached`, `start_time`, `task` and `sla`, and `planned_end_time` is the "Breach time". As written, `where isnull(breach_time)` passes every row and `pct_elapsed` is always null, so the search returns nothing.

There is no `stage="in_progress"` filter and no per-`sys_id` latest reduction, so completed, cancelled or paused SLAs and older snapshots can appear as at-risk. Confirm whether Splunk_TA_snow emits glide_date_time fields as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` strings; if so, the arithmetic against `now()` needs `strptime` first.
SLA breach prediction for ITSM tickets is an operations or observability concern, not Security.

summary: The intent (flag open SLAs that have used at least 80% of their time) is clear and the plain-language explanation is good. However, the implementation and SPL use ServiceNow task_sla field names that do not exist, they recompute an elapsed percentage the SLA engine already provides, and the rest of the prose is generic template text.
